FEATURE: Newcastle’s team sheet is the morning’s hinge
Hull test arrives with Newcastle short of options

The Saturday 10:00am ET meeting at St James’ Park is a team-news fixture before it is anything else. Newcastle’s 19 September read lists eight unavailable players: Anthony Elanga, Jacob Ramsey, Nico Gonzalez, Joelinton, Dan Burn, Amar Dedic, William Osula and Ewen Jaouen. The absence list reaches across the back line, midfield and attack, leaving Matthias Jaissle with a selection problem that the market board cannot solve by itself.

The Newcastle team page read on 19 September lists Elanga, Ramsey, Gonzalez, Joelinton, Burn, Dedic, Osula and Jaouen unavailable; Elanga’s absence is reported at six to eight weeks (BBC Sport, https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/teams/newcastle-united).

Hull’s treatment-room read remains broad: Nobel Mendy is in concussion assessment, Hidemasa Morita is out with an adductor problem and six other players remain listed in the 16 September report (Hull Daily Mail, https://www.hulldailymail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/hull-city-could-without-eight-11156230).

The other Saturday team-news hinge is Tottenham’s return group: Tonali, Porro, Maddison and Udogie are available or returning before Aston Villa (Football London, https://www.football.london/tottenham-hotspur-fc/news/tottenham-injury-news-de-zerbi-34641317.amp; RotoWire, https://www.rotowire.com/soccer/headlines/sandro-tonali-injury-fit-to-face-aston-villa-534289).

RANKINGS_NOTES: Opta and the market disagree most sharply about Chelsea: the Opta Power Rankings have them ninth in the world and only England's fifth-best side, behind Liverpool and Manchester United, while the market treats Chelsea as England's third strongest title contender after a winning start to the season.

Everton are the other clear split. Opta rates them inside the world's top 20 on the strength of last season's underlying numbers, yet the market's list of title contenders runs through Brentford, Aston Villa, Brighton and Newcastle without mentioning Everton at all.

Aston Villa and Newcastle move the other way: the market has pushed both out after summer squad losses, while Opta still keeps them 12th and 11th in the world, i.e. above every English club except the Arsenal-City-Liverpool-United-Chelsea group.
LEAGUES_NOTES: All six European tables are from the opening weeks of 2026-27, so positions are noisy: La Liga has played three rounds, Serie A and Ligue 1 two, the Bundesliga one, and Eredivisie and Primeira Liga clubs have played unequal numbers of games.

Bands follow each competition's current allocation as published alongside the table: four Champions League places in Spain and Italy (plus one Europa and one Conference), and in France, Netherlands, Portugal and Germany the top places include qualifying-round entries rather than guaranteed league-phase spots.

The Bundesliga, Ligue 1, Eredivisie and Primeira Liga are 18-team leagues with two automatic relegations plus a relegation play-off; that play-off place is banded 'playoff' here, so 'playoff' means a promotion/relegation play-off in Europe and MLS Cup Playoffs qualification in MLS.

MLS is the 2026 calendar-year season in its closing stretch, shown as two conferences. The playoff band covers positions 1-9 in each conference: 1-7 enter Round One directly and 8-9 enter the Wild Card matches.
